title: Lighting environmental assessment in enclosed spaces based on emotional model
central_proposition: This study proposes and validates the Check-all-that-apply (CATA), Subjective Coordinate Scale (SCS), and FaceReader (FRE) methods as effective tools for assessing the emotional impact of various lighting environments in enclosed spaces.

concept_definitions.name: Enclosed space
concept_definitions.definition: A space surrounded by a highly restrictive enclosure entity with strong visual and auditory isolation, giving people a sense of domain, security, and privacy.

concept_definitions.name: Emotion
concept_definitions.definition: A kind of emotional tendency associated with changes in patterns of physiological arousal and tending to favorable stimuli or avoiding harmful stimuli.

concept_definitions.name: Discrete emotion model
concept_definitions.definition: Emotion models, also known as basic emotion theory models, represented by theories from Tomkins, Izard, Ekman, and Plutchik, classifying emotions into distinct categories (e.g., happiness, sadness, anger).

concept_definitions.name: Dimensional emotion model
concept_definitions.definition: Emotion models suggesting human emotions have a multidimensional structure, with each dimension (e.g., Valence, Arousal, Dominance) being a characteristic of the emotion.

concept_definitions.name: Valence
concept_definitions.definition: A dimension of emotion representing the degree of pleasantness, ranging from very unhappy to very happy.

concept_definitions.name: Arousal
concept_definitions.definition: A dimension of emotion representing the degree of physiological activation, ranging from very sleepy to very alert.

concept_definitions.name: Check-all-that-apply (CATA)
concept_definitions.definition: A rapid sensory analysis method where participants select descriptive words from a list that appropriately describe their sensory experience of an object or environment.

concept_definitions.name: Subjective Coordinate Scale (SCS)
concept_definitions.definition: A two-dimensional coordinate system (Valence-Arousal) allowing participants to self-report their current emotional state by placing a mark on the scale.

concept_definitions.name: FaceReader (FRE)
concept_definitions.definition: Automated facial emotion recognition software that detects small local facial features and muscle movements (based on FACS) to analyze and predict emotional states.

argument_structure: The paper argues for the validity and utility of CATA, SCS, and FRE by conducting an experiment in a closed laboratory with 6 different lighting settings. It collects subjective self-reports (CATA, SCS) and objective facial expression data (FRE), then statistically analyzes and compares the results to demonstrate the effectiveness and consistency of these methods in assessing emotional responses to lighting.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: The paper leverages existing emotion models (Circumplex Valence-Arousal, PAD) as the theoretical basis for emotional assessment. The implicit causal logic is that specific lighting parameters (CCT, illuminance) influence human emotional states (valence, arousal). The proposed methods (CATA, SCS, FRE) are posited to effectively capture these emotional responses, with FRE specifically operating by analyzing facial muscle movements (FACS) as objective indicators of emotion.

findings.consequent: Subjective emotion assessment of lighting settings
findings.mechanism: Allows participants to quickly and intuitively select descriptive words that match their sensory and emotional experience, reducing answering burden.
findings.quote: The CATA method is a form of questioning used to quickly obtain sensory profiles of products from consumers
findings.empirical_support_cited: Validated through experimental results showing consistent emotional profiles across lighting settings.

findings.consequent: Subjective emotion assessment of lighting settings
findings.mechanism: Enables participants to freely and quantitatively self-report their current emotion state on a two-dimensional Valence-Arousal coordinate system, without losing patience.
findings.quote: This two-dimensional coordinate system... has the advantage of allowing participants to complete the self-report at one time without losing their patience
findings.empirical_support_cited: Validated through experimental results showing consistent emotional profiles across lighting settings.

findings.consequent: Objective emotion assessment (facial expressions) of lighting settings
findings.mechanism: Automatically analyzes facial expressions by detecting minimal muscle movements (FACS) to provide real-time, objective estimates of emotional states (valence, arousal).
findings.quote: FRE detects small local facial features by describing minimal muscle movements through the Facial Action Coding System (FACS)
findings.empirical_support_cited: Validated through experimental results showing effective identification of emotional differences and consistency with subjective reports.

findings.antecedent: Lighting settings (3100 K × 600 lx, 3100 K × 1000 lx, 6500 K × 600 lx)
findings.mechanism: These specific combinations of correlated color temperature (CCT) and illuminance levels create an optimal visual and non-visual environment conducive to positive emotional states.
findings.quote: the 3100 K × 600 lx, 3100 K × 1000 lx and 6500 K × 600 lx lighting settings creating a relaxed, pleasant emotion in participants
findings.empirical_support_cited: CATA and SCS results showed these settings created relaxed, pleasant emotions; FRE results also indicated higher valence.

findings.mechanism: The combination of high CCT and high illuminance can be overstimulating, leading to increased arousal and negative valence.
findings.quote: the 6500 K × 1000 lx setting creating an excited, tense atmosphere
findings.empirical_support_cited: CATA and SCS results showed this setting created an excited, tense atmosphere; FRE results indicated high arousal.

findings.antecedent: Low illumination level settings (3100 K × 250 lx and 6500 K × 250 lx)
findings.consequent: Tired and frustrated emotion in participants
findings.mechanism: Insufficient illuminance, regardless of CCT, can lead to feelings of fatigue and frustration due to inadequate visual and non-visual stimulation.
findings.quote: the low illumination level settings of 3100 K × 250 lx and 6500 K × 250 lx made participants feel tired and frustrated.
findings.empirical_support_cited: CATA and SCS results showed these settings made participants feel tired and frustrated; FRE results indicated low arousal and valence.

findings.consequent: Consistency in subjective emotion assessment results
findings.mechanism: Both methods effectively capture self-reported emotional states, indicating their reliability as subjective assessment tools, despite different interfaces.
findings.quote: The CATA and SCS showed similar results
findings.empirical_support_cited: Experimental results showed similar emotional profiles and conclusions from both CATA and SCS.

findings.consequent: Consistency with participants' subjective emotion reports
findings.mechanism: Objective facial expression analysis aligns with self-reported emotional states, validating FRE as an objective measure that reflects subjective experience.
findings.quote: the FRE was able to effectively identify differences in participants' emotions in response to different lighting settings and was consistent with the results of participants' subjective emotion reports.
findings.empirical_support_cited: Experimental results showed FRE effectively identified emotional differences consistent with subjective reports.

findings.consequent: Quick and accurate orientation of new lighting environments
findings.mechanism: Its simple and intuitive task design reduces participant burden, making it efficient for rapid assessment, especially with large participant numbers.
findings.quote: The CATA method allows for a quick and accurate orientation of a new lighting environment, especially when a large number of participants are required
findings.empirical_support_cited: The method's ease of use and ability to provide clear emotional profiles were demonstrated in the study.

findings.mechanism: The two-dimensional coordinate system allows participants to freely and quantitatively express their nuanced emotional states, providing a more objective reflection of subjective experience.
findings.quote: The SCS method, on the other hand, allows participants to freely select their current emotion and can more objectively reflect their subjective emotions.
findings.empirical_support_cited: The method's ability to capture nuanced emotional states without predefined categories was demonstrated.

findings.consequent: Detection of variability in participants' emotions under different lighting settings
findings.mechanism: Automated analysis of facial expressions provides a sensitive and objective measure capable of identifying subtle changes in emotional states in response to environmental variations.
findings.quote: FRE facial emotion recognition method can effectively detect the variability of participants' emotions under different lighting settings.
findings.empirical_support_cited: The study's objective emotion analysis indicated FRE effectively identified differences in participants' emotions across settings.

findings.antecedent: Different lighting settings (CCT and illuminance combinations)
findings.mechanism: Variations in lighting parameters influence the perceived pleasantness or unpleasantness of the environment, which is reflected in facial expressions.
findings.quote: For the valence analysis, the largest difference was between lighting setting 1 and lighting setting 3, with a mean difference of - 0.0637 (P = 0.025)
findings.empirical_support_cited: Paired samples t-test showed significant differences in valence across various lighting setting pairs (e.g., setting 1 vs 3: mean difference -0.0637, P = 0.025).

findings.antecedent: Different lighting settings (CCT and illuminance combinations)
findings.mechanism: Variations in lighting parameters influence the physiological activation and alertness levels of individuals, which is reflected in facial expressions.
findings.quote: For the arousal value analysis, the largest difference was between lighting setting 1 and lighting setting 3, with a mean difference of 0.0310 (P = 0.000).
findings.empirical_support_cited: Paired samples t-test showed significant differences in arousal across various lighting setting pairs (e.g., setting 1 vs 3: mean difference 0.0310, P = 0.000).

findings.antecedent: Different lighting settings (CCT and illuminance combinations)
findings.mechanism: Lighting parameters influence self-reported emotional pleasantness or unpleasantness.
findings.quote: 6 lighting settings showing significance at the 0.01 level for valence (F = 5.531, P = 0.000)
findings.empirical_support_cited: ANOVA showed significant differences for valence across all lighting settings (F = 5.531, P = 0.000).

findings.antecedent: Different lighting settings (CCT and illuminance combinations)
findings.mechanism: Lighting parameters influence self-reported emotional activation and alertness.
findings.quote: 6 lighting settings showing significance at the 0.01 level for arousal (F = 7.419, P = 0.000)
findings.empirical_support_cited: ANOVA showed significant differences for arousal across all lighting settings (F = 7.419, P = 0.000).

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: Specific lighting combinations will be more effective in stimulating subjective positive emotions in workers within an enclosed environment.
The CATA and SCS methods will yield consistent results in assessing subjective emotions, but will exhibit distinct characteristics in their application.
FRE will prove to be an effective objective tool for emotional assessment of personnel in enclosed space lighting environments.
bridge_warrants: The study's emotional assessment is based on the Circumplex emotion model (Valence-Arousal) and the Pleasure-Arousal-Dominance (PAD) affective model.
FaceReader's operation is grounded in the Facial Action Coding System (FACS) for objective facial emotion analysis.
methodological_critiques: Existing research has not systematically investigated the lighting settings and personnel emotion in enclosed spaces.
limitations: The study's findings are limited by the duration of the experiment, suggesting a need for further investigation into short-term vs. long-term lighting effects on emotion.
The participant demographic (college students) may not fully represent workers in closed spaces, limiting generalizability to specific application scenarios.
The scope of FRE analysis was limited to basic emotion categories; future research could delve deeper into specific expression analysis and chronological emotional changes.

The study only used facial emotion as an objective indicator, suggesting future research should explore multimodal fusion of emotion recognition methods (e.g., speech, gesture, physiological signals).
